metadata.title: Layered-column vertical scattering and tomographic resolution analysis for L-band radar sounding of sea ice (v2.0)
metadata.description: A horizontally layered snow, sea ice, slush and seawater column is built from field-derived parameters. Brine volume follows Cox and Weeks (1983), brine permittivity Stogryn and Desai (1985), and effective sea-ice permittivity a Polder-van Santen mixture with a single effective depolarization factor constrained simultaneously by accepted cold first-year-ice penetration depths at L-band and C-band. Interface returns follow first-order small-perturbation scattering with an exponential correlation spectrum. Acquisitions are modelled as samples of the vertical wavenumber, verified against exact two-way ray tracing; profiles are estimated by beamforming, Capon and MUSIC, and bounded by a conditional two-reflector Cramer-Rao analysis. A Monte Carlo sub-cell model adds footprint-scale lateral heterogeneity and detector operating characteristics under a deformed-ice confounder.This package extends the semi-empirical forward model archived at doi:10.5281/zenodo.19829367. That earlier deposit remains the archive of record for the Commentary and is unchanged by this release. The archival v1.0 module is retained here verbatim, with two documented defects noted in CHANGELOG.md that do not affect the published figure. Requires Python 3.10 or later with numpy, scipy and matplotlib. All random seeds are fixed, so runs are deterministic. MIT licence.

hits.title: Layered-column vertical scattering and tomographic resolution analysis for L-band radar sounding of sea ice (v2.0)

Contributors

  • Chris Kees @cekees
  • Arnob Barua @abarua-ce
  • Darsh Nathawani @nathawani
  • linojr @linojr
  • jhcollins @jhcollins

New features

  • Improved CutFEM and IFEM support for higher order FEM and multiphase models
  • Improved FCT support for Richards' equation
  • New models for multiphase and multicomponent flows with FCT schemes
  • New packaging and CI tooling:
    • Conda Forge
    • Spack
    • Github Actions

Issues fixed/closed

  • erdc/proteus#1274 — Richards-FCT. Relative hydraulic conductivity and moisture content can now be output alongside pressure head. The release adds the pore-size-distribution closures with explicit kr models (van Genuchten/Mualem, Brooks-Corey/Burdine, Brooks-Corey/Mualem, Gardner) and theta at the quadrature points. Reported by, and fixed by, Arnob Barua.

  • erdc/proteus#1280 — Does not build or install on macOS (Apple Silicon). Resolved by conda-forge packaging rather than by this repository. All four dependencies the issue named are no longer blockers: pychrono 10.0.0, scorec 4.2.1 and tetgen 1.6.0 all publish osx-arm64, and daetk — which still has no osx-arm64 build — is no longer a proteus dependency at all. A proteus osx-arm64 package exists.

  • erdc/proteus#1018 — conda-forge package. Exists, building for linux-64, linux-aarch64, osx-64 and osx-arm64.

  • erdc/proteus#985 — fix incorrect assertions in SW2DCV and GN_SW2DCV. The always-true assert (cond, "msg") tuples were fixed before 1.8.3, in 203f398a.

  • erdc/proteus#941 — Error when computing max wave speed for SW2DCV. Also fixed before 1.8.3; SW2DCV.h takes fmax(fabs(lambda1), fabs(lambda3)) at the tag.

  • NumPy >= 2.0 compatibility in SpatialTools.unique_rows — np.unique now shapes inverse like the structured-dtype view rather than flat, which broke downstream fancy-indexing.

  • mprans/SpatialTools.assembleAuxiliaryVariables tested a chrono boundaryFlags array for truthiness; now tests .size == 0.

  • many latent issues in the contributed tests fixed

metadata.title: Reproducibility archive for conditioning-controlled retrieval of broadband land surface temperature and emissivity from paired ground-based longwave irradiance measurements
metadata.description: This archive provides the frozen Version 12b scientific reproducibility materials associated with the manuscript “Conditioning-controlled retrieval of broadband land surface temperature and emissivity from paired ground-based longwave irradiance measurements” (egusphere-2026-858), by Collins Mito. It contains the authoritative scientific code, publication-generation code, and frozen machine-readable derived outputs used for the field and physics-based known-truth synthetic validation reported in the accepted manuscript. The archive preserves the established retrieval formulation, including the fixed eight-update Newton–Raphson implementation. Raw third-party SURFRAD and BSRN observations are not redistributed in this archive; they remain available from their respective public data services. This record supports traceability and reproducibility of the published analyses and derived results.

hits.title: Reproducibility archive for conditioning-controlled retrieval of broadband land surface temperature and emissivity from paired ground-based longwave irradiance measurements

metadata.title: Code for "Quantifying the responses of AI precipitation forecast errors to reanalysis errors using analysis of covariance"
metadata.description: This repository archives the code supporting the manuscript “Quantifying the responses of AI precipitation forecast errors to reanalysis errors using analysis of covariance". It includes scripts and notebooks for generating GraphCast forecasts, aggregating precipitation to 1426 CAMELS-SPAT catchments, identifying extreme precipitation, calculating forecast and reanalysis errors, fitting the ANCOVA model and reproducing the figures. A frozen copy of the official GraphCast implementation released by Google DeepMind, together with the model weights and normalization statistics used in this study, is also included to facilitate reproducibility.

metadata.title: music: extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements
metadata.description:
Extreme-fidelity synthesis of musical elements, based on the MASS framework: psychophysical descriptions of musical elements in LPCM audio, expressed as equations and corresponding Python routines. State is updated at every sample, so a rendered sound is as close as it can be to the mathematical model that describes it.

The package covers synthesis of notes and their variation (vibrato, glissando, FM and AM, ADSR envelopes, the six noise colours), filters and their design, spatialisation by interaural time and intensity difference and by measured head-related transfer functions, reverberation, music theory (the diatonic modes, the minor scales, triads and tetrads, the intervals and their names, the harmonic series), permutation groups and change-ringing peals, and a sensory-stimulation toolkit whose stimuli each name the technique they implement in the SSTIM vocabulary.

Its correspondence with the published framework is measured rather than asserted. Every routine is compared with the MASS reference implementation, and separately against the numbered equations of the article itself: 26 of the reference's 35 routines are reproduced sample for sample and the rest diverge for stated reasons, and 45 of the article's 47 labelled equations are checked by a test, which is all of those a test could settle. Where the article, the reference implementation and this package disagree, the disagreement is recorded with the evidence for it.

metadata.title: fabtwin: learned generative process twins for yield-aware inverse design of multilayer optics
metadata.description:
Real-data release: the pipeline the paper names as its essential next step -- a process twin trained and scored on a lab's own in-situ monitoring traces -- is now a documented, validated pathway. The twins never see a simulator by construction; this release adds the ingestion, quality control and honest scoring that make real (recipe, outcome) data drop in seamlessly.

Trace ingestion and validation (fabtwin.data)

  • load_traces_csv / save_traces_csv on a documented tidy trace-file contract (one row per run and layer: run, layer, t_recipe_um, n_recipe, t_fab_um, n_fab) with an exact round trip, and refusal -- not guessing -- for malformed files: wrong header, layer gaps, duplicate layers, ragged runs. Standard-library csv on NumPy; no pandas dependency.
  • validate_traces separates two kinds of trouble in real data: structural problems (non-finite values, non-positive thicknesses, shape mismatches) RAISE; plausibility findings (values beyond documented screening thresholds that usually mean a unit mix-up) are RETURNED for the user's judgment -- a lab's outliers are never silently dropped, because the heavy tail is precisely what the twin is for.

Held-out twin fidelity (fabtwin.fidelity)

The paper scores twins against a held-out ground-truth simulator; real data has no such oracle. The honest substitute: fit on part of the traces, score against the held-out rest, on the same statistic types as the paper's Table I(A):

  • moment_errors: pooled mean / covariance / correlation discrepancies;
  • distribution_distances: |d mean|, |d P|, |d CVaR| (the exact conventions of fabtwin.risk) and the 1-D Wasserstein distance;
  • induced_merits + twin_fidelity_report: the merit distributions the error samples induce on a calibration design bank, through the exact solver, averaged over the bank.

Anchors asserted, not stated: every distance is exactly zero against self; W1 equals SciPy's independent implementation exactly; tail statistics are bitwise the risk conventions; a deliberately mean-shifted twin scores strictly worse than a fitted one on held-out data; and the complete workflow -- CSV in, validate, split, fit, held-out fidelity report, CVaR robustification -- runs end to end in the tests.

Honest scope, stated plainly

A held-out split certifies the twin against your fab's recorded behavior; it cannot certify error patterns the tool has never logged. The paper's yield-gain numbers are established within its virtual setting. In production the twin needs periodic retraining on fresh traces as the tool drifts -- the paper's own Applicability caveat, reproduced in the README rather than hidden.

52 tests, Python 3.10-3.13. Install: pip install -U fabtwin.
metadata.notes: If you use this software, please cite it together with the associated paper.

metadata.title: nvrecon: physics-informed magnetization reconstruction from NV magnetometry maps
metadata.description: Python package nvrecon: physics-informed reconstruction of a thin-film magnetization from a single nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry map. The reconstruction minimizes a relative L2 misfit between the measured NV-projected stray field and the field of a candidate magnetization, plus a weighted micromagnetic energy, with the NV standoff optimized jointly. Forward model: NeuralMag cell-averaged finite differences on JAX with Fourier-space upward continuation. Kernels: L-BFGS in spherical coordinates and Riemannian Adam . The README gives example commands; the parameters of every published run are in the config.json files of the data record (Phys. Rev. Lett., DOI 10.1103/nc5g-3yw9). The measured NV maps and masks are included under CC BY 4.0; all published reconstructions are in the data record 10.5281/zenodo.22674823.
